text: So let us leave behind the elementary teaching about Christ and press on toward maturity, not laying again the foundation: repentance from dead works and faith in God,
instruction about baptisms and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
And this we will do, if God permits.
For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and shared in the Holy Spirit,
who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come,
and who have then fallen away—it is impossible to restore them again to repentance, since they are crucifying the Son of God all over again and holding him up to contempt.
For land that drinks in the rain that falls on it again and again, and produces a crop useful to those for whom it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God.
But if it yields thorns and thistles, it is worthless and close to being cursed, and in the end it will be burned.
Yet even though we speak this way, dear friends, we are convinced of better things concerning you—things that belong to salvation.
For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown for his name in having served his holy people, and in serving them still.

versions.text: For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown for his name in serving the saints, as you continue to serve them.
versions.explanation: The Greek pairs an aorist participle (past service) with a present participle (ongoing service). The current rendering blurs the past service into the same phrase; making both explicit preserves the contrast and reads well aloud.

text: But we long for each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, so that your hope may come to full assurance,

versions.text: But we long for each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, so that your hope may be fully realized,
versions.explanation: πληροφορία denotes 'full assurance/certainty' rather than realization or fulfillment. 'Fully realized' shifts the sense toward the hope being obtained rather than the believer's confidence in it being complete.

text: so that you will not become sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
When God made his promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater for him to swear by, he swore by himself,
saying, "I will surely bless you and surely multiply you."
And so, after waiting patiently, Abraham received what was promised.
People swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath serves as confirmation, putting an end to all dispute.
So when God wanted to show the heirs of the promise even more clearly how unchangeable his purpose was, he guaranteed it with an oath,
so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to him for refuge might have a strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us.
This hope we have as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It reaches within, behind the curtain,
where Jesus has entered on our behalf as forerunner, having become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
